newsitem.title: USA: Green groups criticize World Trade Organization.
newsitem.headline: Green groups criticize World Trade Organization.

text.p: Three major U.S. environmental groups on Monday called the World Trade Organisation's environmental positions a failure that has heightened conflicts between trade and environmental protections.

As trade ministers in Singapore began their first meeting since the WTO was launched in 1994, the Sierra Club, the World Wildlife Fund and the National Wildlife Federation said two years of environmental negotiations at the WTO have been "an almost total failure."

The environmental groups said a lack of reforms in WTO trade policies that dealt with the environment jeopardised international treaties such as the protocol to protect the atmosphere's ozone layer and conventions to protect endangered species and control trade in hazardous waste.

"The WTO is trying to expand its power to sit in judgment of environmental treaty systems. They appear to be picking fights that could damage both the WTO and the environment," David Schorr of the World Wildlife Fund said in a statement.
A report the WTO's Committee on Trade and Environment (CTE) is to present to the ministers "does not contain a single significant recommendation for environmental reform at the WTO," Schorr said.
"Rather than reducing tensions between trade and environment, the WTO is taking us down the path of confrontation over environmental issues," Schorr said.
The environmental committee of the WTO was formed to see that international trade rules do not compromise countries' efforts to protect the environment and encourage sustainable development.
